findings.location: sections/20-rend-the-heavens.tex lines 114-119 (and the question at line 130, answered at lines 130-151); against sections/40-clay-and-faithful-potter.tex lines 113-117
findings.problem: Lane 1 says of Augustine on the Alleluia verse: 'Augustine's comment is four words, salutare tuum, Christum tuum: "Thy salvation, that is, Thy Christ" (84.9).' That is false. The source is the verified, bound passage record passage.augustine.enarrationes-in-psalmos.latin-migne-corpus-corporum-wikisource-web-2026-09-05.84-9. En. in Ps. 84.9 is a long section on this verse. It: (a) opens 'Hoc est quod cantavimus' (this is what we sang); (b) identifies the salvation with Christ; (c) asks the very question lane 1 asks: 'Jam quidem dedit nobis Christum suum: adhuc illi tamen dicamus, Da nobis Christum tuum ... Dedit enim nobis Christum, sed hominem: quem nobis dedit hominem, eum ipsum nobis daturus est Deum' ('He has already given us his Christ; yet let us still say to him, Give us thy Christ ... For he gave us Christ, but as man; the one he gave us as man he will give us as God'); (d) closes by asking to see Christ 'non quomodo illum viderunt Judaei, et crucifixerunt, sed quomodo illum vident Angeli, et gaudent'. Lane 3 (40:113-117) quotes another sentence of the same section, so the study contradicts itself about it. The misreport costs the interpretation its strongest patristic step. 20:130 asks 'If the cry was answered at Bethlehem, why does the Church pray it again?' The lane answers only from Cyril and from the study's own inference (20:140-144). Yet one of its carrying authors answers that question in his own words, on the verse the Alleluia sings. The Oxford English the study uses for Augustine abridges this part of §6 with an ellipsis. The bound Latin is complete.
findings.required_result: Do not describe the comment as four words. Report what Augustine says at 84.9 (§6 in the Oxford translation), and credit him only with what he says. Where the Oxford English omits the passage, translate the bound Latin and mark the translation as the study's. Where the lane asks why the Church still prays for a coming already granted (20:130-151), give Augustine's answer as his: Christ has been given, and the Church still asks 'Give us thy Christ', because he was given as man and the same Christ is still to be given as God, to be seen as the angels see him. Keep the citation form consistent with 40:117.

findings.location: sections/30-watch-at-the-door.tex, whole section (no Alleluia verse, Prayer over the Offerings or solemn blessing); sections/40-clay-and-faithful-potter.tex, whole section (no Preface); research/production-review.md lines 219-222
findings.problem: The study-review contract requires each interpretation to engage 'the entire appointed formulary'. The three-document profile requires each to 'let every appointed element contribute, including orations and minor chants'. Under the profile, 'A text the interpretation touches lightly gets a clause, not a manufactured role.' The second interpretation never mentions the Alleluia verse (Ps 85 (84):8), the Prayer over the Offerings or the solemn blessing. The third never mentions the Preface. A word search of both files confirms these absences. The component contract declares all twelve element keys for both lanes. The production audit records the omission as policy: 'Texts an interpretation does not use are left out of it or given a clause in its four senses' (production-review lines 219-222). That follows one sentence of STU-001's required result ('A text the interpretation does not use is left out rather than given a use'). The same finding also said 'Every element must still be treated'. The contract does not allow an element to be left out.
findings.required_result: Give each missing element at least a clause in its interpretation, where the argument or the four senses can use what the text says, without assigning it a role. For example: (a) In the second interpretation, beside Chrysostom's 'continually in virtuous action' or Gregory's 'keeps by works what he believes': 'The Prayer over the Offerings asks that what God grants their devotion to accomplish in this passing time become the reward of eternal redemption.' (b) In its anagogical sense, after the Preface: '... and the solemn blessing, where it is used, asks eternal life for those who await him when he comes again in majesty.' (c) In its moral sense: '... he asks, in the Alleluia verse, to be shown God's mercy and given his salvation.' (d) In the third interpretation, beside Aquinas's fellowship 'in futuro per participationem gloriae', or in its anagogical sense: 'The Preface speaks of the same future: at the second coming those who now wait will receive openly what was promised.' Correct the production audit's statement of policy.

findings.location: sections/00-opening.tex lines 32-34 and 48-65; sections/20-rend-the-heavens.tex lines 7-15, 160-162 and 171-179; sections/30-watch-at-the-door.tex lines 12-22; sections/40-clay-and-faithful-potter.tex lines 12-20; sections/50-comparison.tex lines 4-10, 45-48 and 52-55; sections/05-appointed-texts.tex lines 59-60; sections/10-texts-in-setting.tex lines 161-163
findings.problem: Recurring register pattern under guidance/editorial.md. 'Say it once' forbids restating 'a thesis in a lead, a closer and a summary' and carrying 'a phrase from section to section as a refrain'. 'Plain is not flat' names 'a run of names with one-line verdicts' and 'a fixed formula ... repeated from paragraph to paragraph' as defects. Instances: (1) Author rosters given twice. 00:48-65 strings every carrying author with a one-line verdict. Each lane lead then repeats its roster nearly word for word: 00:51-52 and 20:11-12, 'Augustine reads the psalm as a song of the Lord's coming'; 00:52-53 and 20:12-13, 'Cyril of Jerusalem teaches that Christ comes twice'; 00:54-56 and 30:12-14, 'Jerome and John Chrysostom, commenting on [Matthew] ..., say why the hour is hidden'; 00:59-60 and 30:18-19, 'Bede, [commenting] on Mark, assigns the watch to the [porter/doorkeeper], the servants and every heart'; 00:61-65 and 40:12-19, the same claims about Jerome, Aquinas and Chrysostom. (2) One formula ends each lead and credits the lane's thesis to the authors jointly: 20:13 'Put together, their readings make the cry a prayer ...'; 30:19 'Taken together, they make the command to watch hold ...'; 40:19 'Put together, what they say rests the hope ... on who God is'. None of the authors states those syntheses; the three-document profile forbids the related form 'these Fathers carry it: <thesis>'. The comparison states the three theses again (50:4-10), and lane 1's a further time (50:45-48). (3) Observations carried as refrains: the participle venienti 'as one already on his way' or 'on the road' at 05:59-60, 10:161-163 and 20:160-162; the absence of 'thou didst come down' from the US English at 00:32-34, 20:173-175 and 50:52-55. (4) Lane 1's 'Where this interpretation strains' (20:171-179) restates the body. Its first strain is 00:32-34, its second 20:61-74, its third 20:166-169. It ends on process narration, 'They are read together here because ...', an isolated residue of the STU-002 pattern.
findings.required_result: Say each thing once, and state each lane's thesis once, in plain words, as the study's conclusion from the reasoning it reports. Rewrites: (a) 00:48-65: keep the three questions and drop the rosters that the lane leads repeat: 'Three questions rise from these texts. The first is whether the prophet's cry has been answered, and if so, how the Church can still pray it. The second is why Christ hides the hour of his coming, and to whom his command is spoken when most who hear it will die before the end. The third is on what ground a people that has strayed can hope to be found blameless on the day.' Alternatively, keep the rosters here and open each lane on its question and its texts. (b) 30:19-22: 'Taken together, they make the command to watch hold for the whole time between the two comings: always, ...' becomes 'The command to watch therefore holds for the whole time between the two comings: always, because the hour is hidden, and for everyone, because each one's death brings the end to him.' Treat 20:13-15 and 40:19-20 the same way, each in its own words, without a shared formula. (c) 20:160-162: 'The Collect, too, speaks of Christ as already on his way: it asks for the will to go out to meet him venienti, as he comes.' becomes 'The Collect asks for the will to go out to meet Christ as he comes (venienti).' Keep the observation about the participle in one place, section 05 or section 10. (d) 20:171-179: keep only what the body has not already said, for example 'None of the Fathers cited sets Isaiah's cry beside Mark's parable.' Cut 'They are read together here because ...'. (e) The comparison (50:4-10, 45-48) compares the interpretations and does not restate each thesis.

findings.location: sections/10-texts-in-setting.tex lines 209-211; sections/20-rend-the-heavens.tex lines 201-203; sections/30-watch-at-the-door.tex lines 150-152; sections/40-clay-and-faithful-potter.tex lines 207-208
findings.problem: The Prayer after Communion asks that the mysteries profit those who receive them. It gives the reason as a statement: through them God already teaches (iam nunc instituis) those who walk among passing things to love what is heavenly and cling to what lasts. propers/verified.md, 05:280-284 and 00:118-122 say so. Four other places turn the reason into a petition: 10:209-211 'the two halves together ask that through the mysteries God teach his people'; 20:202 'the Prayer after Communion asks to hold ... to what lasts'; 30:150 'asks God to teach the same thing'; 40:207 'asks God to teach his people to love what is heavenly'. At 10:209-211 the misreading also hides what the section is tracing: both Verona sources ask (instituant; Da nobis ...), and the Missal's prayer says that God already does it.
findings.required_result: In all four places, describe the prayer as section 05 does: it asks that the mysteries profit them, since by them God already teaches them, among passing things, to love what is heavenly and hold to what lasts. For example, 30:150-152: 'The Prayer after Communion says that by the mysteries God already teaches those who live among things that pass to love what is heavenly and hold to what lasts.'

findings.problem: The word 'first' names two different senses of Aquinas on Descendisti. At 00:50 ('reads the same past tense first of the Lord's coming down to free Israel from Egypt'), 20:11 ('puts another before it') and 20:70 ('for Aquinas it is first a memory') it means the sense he prefers, which he lists last ('Vel melius, secundum litteralem sensum', [85024]). At 20:199 'Aquinas's first sense, the past put for the future' is the judgment, the first sense he lists; at 20:191 'Aquinas's second sense' is the descent into the womb. So the opening says that Aquinas reads the verb first of Egypt, and the four senses say that his first sense is the judgment. Separately, 20:59-60 explains praeteritum pro futuro with 'as prophets speak of what is certain to come'. Aquinas's comment has no such clause, and in a sentence reporting him the explanation reads as his.
findings.required_result: Use one wording for each meaning: 'the sense he prefers' (or 'his literal sense') for Egypt, and 'the first/second sense he lists' for the order. For example, 20:199 '(Cyril; the first sense Aquinas lists, the past put for the future)', and 00:50 'Thomas Aquinas prefers, as the literal sense, the Lord's coming down to free Israel from Egypt'. Cut the explanation at 20:60, or mark it as the study's.

findings.problem: (a) 20:166-167 says that, in the Gospel, 'Gregory the Great and Bede read him [Mark's master gone abroad] as Christ ascended'. Gregory does not comment on Mark 13:34. He identifies the traveller of Matthew 25:14 (Hom. in Ev. 9.1, 'Quis itaque iste homo est qui peregre proficiscitur, nisi Redemptor noster, qui in ea carne quam assumpserat abiit in coelum?', tracked Latin) and, on Luke 12, the master gone to the wedding (13.2). Bede applies Gregory's sentence to Mark, as 30:160-162 correctly says. (b) The allegorical sense at 30:219-221 reads: 'The man gone abroad is Christ ascended, who left the Church in the body and never without his presence (Gregory, and Bede after him)'. This credits Gregory with Bede's own clause 'quam tamen nunquam divinae praesidio praesentiae destituit' (Bede, tracked Latin line 404). That clause is not in Hom. 9.1, as the study's own note at 30:160-162 and the Bede binding in research/source-bindings.toml record.
findings.required_result: (a) '... and Bede, using Gregory's words on the traveller of Matthew 25, reads him as Christ ascended.' (b) 'The man gone abroad is Christ ascended (Gregory on Matthew's traveller, and Bede on Mark's), who left the Church in the body and never without his presence (Bede); ...'

findings.problem: The apparatus lists the links between texts that the authors themselves draw, and says: 'Jerome and Aquinas link the petition of Isaiah 63:17 to the psalm's converte nos'. Neither cites the psalm there. Jerome reads the petition as 'Convertere, ait, Domine, sive converte nos' (PL 24 cols. 643-644, page image). Aquinas sets Psalm 90 (89):13 and Lamentations 5:21 beside convertere ([85023], fetched page). The body is correct (40:55-62): converte nos is Jerome's reading of the petition, and it is also the wording of the psalm's refrain, which is the study's observation. The apparatus moves the study's link into the authors' column, the very distinction the paragraph exists to keep.
findings.required_result: Restate as the body does, for example: 'Jerome reads the petition of Isaiah 63:17 also as converte nos, "turn us", and Aquinas sets Lamentations 5:21 beside it.' Count the link to the responsorial psalm's refrain among the study's own.

findings.problem: After Bede's doorkeeper as 'the order of pastors and spiritual rulers', the lane brings in the Communion Antiphon through Augustine: 'Augustine speaks as one such pastor when he preaches on the verse the Communion Antiphon sings ...: he has sown, and he asks that God give increase'. Augustine's remark (En. in Ps. 84.15, Oxford §12; the quotation checks) is about preaching and God's increase, not about keeping watch at the door. The link to Bede's doorkeeper is the study's, and it gives the antiphon a role inside Bede's allegory. This is the manufactured-role form that STU-001 removed with the roll calls, surviving once in the body. It is isolated, so advisory.
findings.required_result: Give the Communion Antiphon a clause without placing Augustine inside Bede's allegory. For example: 'Augustine, preaching on the verse the Communion Antiphon sings, "our earth shall yield her fruit", asks that God give increase to the seed he has sown in his hearers (84.15; §12 in the Oxford translation).' Or give the antiphon a clause in the four senses instead.

observations.note: The research record still says the people pray that God come down 'as he once did at Sinai and in Egypt (Aquinas's preferred literal sense)'. Sinai is not in Aquinas's preferred sense ([85024]: Egypt; Exod. 4; Ps 17). research/production-review.md lines 298-304 records this for its owner, and the study no longer repeats it. The file is outside REVIEW_SCOPE and is not raised here.

A crude word count of sections 00-50 at this iteration is about 13,500, in line with the audit's 13,600 from the proof. That is above the profile's 6,000-10,000 planning range, which is not a quota. The content gate run for this review passed; its output is <worker-scratch>/workers/study-review-1/study-check.txt.

summary: Cold review of the expansive study src/claude/liturgy/roman-rite/postconciliar/roman-missal-third-edition-en-us-2011/propers/temporal/pc-s01-first-sunday-of-advent-year-b (sections 00, 05, 10, 20, 30, 40, 50 and 90, generation-metadata.tex and research/production-review.md read in full; section 85 and the generated appendix not reviewed). The three interpretations are distinct and each has its own four senses and at least two Fathers who contribute reasoning. The iteration-0 blocking findings STU-001 to STU-009 and advisories STU-010 to STU-014 are repaired in substance. Two isolated residues are filed under STU-017(4) and STU-022. Evidence checked at its loci: Aquinas, Super Isaiam c. 63-64 [85023]-[85024], on a fresh corpusthomisticum.org fetch matching the registered SHA-256; Aquinas, Super I ad Corinthios c. 1 lect. 1 [86234], also fetched and hash-matched; Jerome, In Isaiam XVII, PL 24 cols. 643-648, on Internet Archive page images; Augustine, Ep. 199.1.1-3, augustinus.it Latin; Augustine, En. in Ps. 84.9 and 84.15 (Latin passage records) and 24.2, 79.1-3, 79.9 and 84 §§6 and 12 (tracked Oxford English); Gregory, Hom. in Ev. 9.1 and 13.2-6, and Bede on Mark 13:32-37 (tracked Latin); Chrysostom on 1 Cor, Hom. 2 (passage record) and on Matthew, Hom. 77 (NPNF); Cyril, Catechesis 15.1; Bellarmine on Psalms 24, 79 and 84. The content gate (_proper_study.py check, content phase) passes. Consequential-difficulty test: (1) Aquinas [85024] on Descendisti. The study reports his three senses and his preference 'Vel melius, secundum litteralem sensum' for the descent from Egypt accurately, and 20:58-74 teaches the Jerome-Aquinas question intelligibly. Pass, apart from a gloss and the word 'first' (STU-019). (2) Jerome col. 647, 'Ordo praeposterus ... tantum salvabimur misericordia'. Pass. (3) Augustine Ep. 199.1.3, the command to all because each one's last day is the world's. Pass. (4) Augustine En. in Ps. 84.9. Fail: it is misreported as four words, and the passage's own answer to lane 1's central question is dropped (STU-015). Limits: the US Lectionary English, the approved Missal English and the Missal Latin of the orations were not seen; for these the study's claims were checked against propers/verified.md and research/context.md. Not every quotation was re-read. No print or web artifact was built. Verdict: CHANGES_REQUIRED, on three blocking findings, all repair_target study: STU-015, Augustine misreported; STU-016, the Alleluia verse, Prayer over the Offerings and solemn blessing are absent from interpretation 2 and the Preface from interpretation 3; STU-017, a recurring 'say it once' register pattern of duplicated author rosters, a shared 'Put/Taken together' thesis formula and refrains. Five advisories (STU-018 to STU-022).
